summary: Early-1930s Aermotor MC-39 tower on the Navajo Indian Reservation, registered in 2002 as still active; no later record of its condition or staffing was found.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-39 tower with a 7 x 7 ft metal cab
facts.status_note: Described as still active when registered in 2002; no later status found.

staffing.status: no staffing described in the 2002 register; no later staffing record found

access.note: The register places the tower on the Navajo Indian Reservation and names the reservation as administrator. The sources give no visiting rule.

facts.agency: Navajo Indian Reservation (administrator); Bureau of Indian Affairs (cooperator)

events.note: Early 1930s per the NHLR entry, which gives no exact year; 1930 is a placeholder for that decade

evidence.supports: one of the early towers on the Navajo reservation; still active when registered
evidence.quote: One of the early towers on the Navajo reservation, Piney Hill Lookout is still active.

evidence.supports: 81 ft Aermotor MC-39 tower with 7x7 metal cab, built early 1930s
evidence.quote: The 81’ Aermotor MC-39 tower with 7’x7’ metal cab was constructed in the early 1930’s on an 8102’ mountaintop.

evidence.supports: administered by the Navajo Indian Reservation
Bureau of Indian Affairs as cooperator
listed as a standing tower with NHLR US 439, AZ 35
evidence.quote: Piney Hill Apache 35.76133 -109.16833 Tower Standing NHLR US 439, AZ 35

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, and the history is from a 2002 register entry. Two web searches found no builder, date, staffing or fire history beyond the register. The register gives two mountaintop heights (8,102 ft in the description, 8,113 ft in the elevation line); the record keeps 8,113 ft (2,473 m). The 1930 build year is a decade placeholder, not a source year. No visiting rule is stated in the sources, so the access level is 'unknown'. Current status is unverified; FFLA's 'Standing' does not say the tower is staffed.
